about: Two config defaults the Go library used to differ on (Python 0.7.1 / Go v0.3.0). Since Go v0.3.0 BOTH libraries default enforcement.enabled and credit_grant.reset_on_downgrade to true when a config FILE omits them (Python always did; Go used false before v0.3.0). For each config document: `warnings` — the exact texts both libraries print for these two keys (Python default_divergence_warnings(config); Go the matching entries of LoadConfig(file).Warnings()), in this order; `effective` — the values both libraries run with. Byte-identical copy in ab0t-quota/tests/ and ab0t-quota-go/testdata/.
enforcement_enabled_unset: enforcement.enabled is not set: the default is now true (limits enforced); it was false (EVERY request allowed) in the Go library before v0.3.0 — set it explicitly to keep the old Go behaviour ("enforcement": {"enabled": false}) or to silence this warning ("enforcement": {"enabled": true})
reset_on_downgrade_unset_template: tier "{tier_id}": credit_grant.reset_on_downgrade is not set: the default is now true (the grant's balance is reset when the org moves to a lower tier); it was false in the Go library before v0.3.0 — set it explicitly to keep the old Go behaviour ("reset_on_downgrade": false) or to silence this warning
